While the kush female in this cross, Deadhead OG, contributes a long-lasting body high and an abbreviated flowering time, this phenotype is dominated by its male parent, Tom Hill Haze. Originally sourced from Sam the Skunkman’s stock by Tom Hill himself, the legendary Tom Hill Haze strain has established itself as a mainstay among cannabis breeders and gardeners since the 1990’s. A well-respected grower and breeder in the NorCal region who has been working with the cannabis plant for decades, Tom Hill specializes in the preservation of pure lines and offers seeds and hybrids of heritage cannabis varieties.

Our phenotype of Deadhead OG x Tom Hill Haze is a towering plant with a tremendous growth rate. She can double the size of other plants in the same amount of vegetative time. Buds stack and form significant colas, requiring considerable support. Complex smells of haze are ever-present, maybe best described as an herbaceous ammonia. The herbs and tea leaves meld with a slight lemony citrus and eventually give way to a hardwood floor cleaner aroma of bleach. As to be expected, an uptick in energy and increased mood are commonly felt when consuming this variety. The Deadhead OG x Tom Hill Haze is sure to excite those nostalgic senses of prior decades’ Haze invasion.

Though pheno-hunting is always something of a lottery, we often seem to hit the jackpot with Crystal Rose Seed Co.’s genetics. Producing winners like Pie Eyed, Wave Runners, and Watermelon Otai, their complex, one-of-a-kind crosses always have us coming back for more, and Grape Crepe is no different.

Prior to the creation of Grape Crepe, Crystal Rose had the opportunity to work with MegaRaw’s brand-building, in-house selected phenotype of Pie Dough, and he crossed it with his own Pie Eyed selection to create Pie Dough Bx1. He then crossed Pie Dough Bx1 with Grape Pie Wedding Crasher, a male known for its abundant resin and grape terps, to create Grape Crepe. Our cultivation team has selected two phenotypes of Grape Crepe: one for flower and the other for solventless extracts, and we have found this cultivar to be a wild improvement on the grape category as a whole.

Opening a jar of our flower phenotype, Grape Crepe #61, launches a purple wave of grape juice and grape candy streaked with a subtle gassy note – an aroma that translates impeccably to flavor with vaporization or combustion. A balanced combination of stress-melting relaxation and uplifting euphoria is consistent with its lineage of Pie Dough, Grape Pie, Wedding Cake, and Purple Punch.

783.desc: RAW Tips are made on an antique Fourdrinier paper machine. Whereas RAW papers are made in Alcoy Spain, we only have machines to produce thin paper in Alcoy. For the thick tipping paper we had to travel to an old paper mill in Northern China that was still using an original Fourdrinier. This was the only place we could find that still had one of these old machines in use, which we needed to make the special long-fiber paper for RAW tips. Want to know more? Modern paper mills use small-structure cellulose to make paper. The original paper mills used fiber instead. For tipping paper to perform best, it needs to be made from fiber – not just boiled cellulose. Fiber-based tips roll smooth AND have enough structural rigidity to both keep its shape in your mouth AND to not dissolve. There are precious few of the original Fourdrinier paper machines in use because they’re antiques and expensive to operate. We were lucky to find this old mill, it’s the only one in the world that can produce RAW tips to our specifications.
